_notes.pages: Word-card choice: 'splash' (p1) is the book's own gate word (RAW n=53 words: ['splash']) and its first printed occurrence, so it anchors p1's card. p2 ('A big splash.') introduces 'big' -- the book's own escalation word (small splash -> big splash), a clean new card. p3 ('Splash in the tub.') introduces 'tub', a concrete, easily-pictured noun (and confirmed present in docs/picture-bank/photos/tub/tub.jpg for cross-checking); the alternative new word 'in' was passed over as a bare preposition with no picture-bank anchor. p4 ('Splash, splash, splash!') introduces no new vocabulary at all -- pure repetition for comic effect, exactly like dp-the-cat-sat.json's page 4 ('A cat on a cat on a cat!'), which faced the identical problem and solved it by borrowing a word first printed on the following page. Following that precedent exactly: 'cat' (first printed on p5, 'The cat is wet!') was assigned to p4 instead, since p4's picture is the clearest, most energetic view of the cat mid-splash -- pedagogically apt, still in-book vocabulary, and keeps all 5 cards distinct. p5 then keeps its own new word 'wet', the story's punchline and clearly depicted end-state (soggy, dripping cat).

The 5 true items are drawn straight from the book's own 5 pages (imageArt = p1.jpg..p5.jpg), one tailored question per page describing exactly what that page's picture and text show (a splash / the splash is big / a tub / the cat splashing again and again / the cat wet), mirroring dp-the-cat-sat.json's page-specific true-question style. Per the 2026-07-30 ruling, false-item words are not restricted to prior-week vocabulary -- picked for clear falseness relative to this specific book instead.
